correctness.rationale: In RESULT.md lines 43–78, the cube is invariant and the nonnegative cross-derivatives give comparison with the two homogeneous scalar extremal solutions, also for reducible W and mixed-side starts. The scalar field g(y)=tanh(2y)/2−y is restoring on either side. Its cubic and quintic terms give (y⁻²)'=8/3−64/(15 y⁻²)+O(y⁴); first y⁻²=(8/3)t+O(log t), then the derivative after subtraction of the linear and log terms has an integrable O(log t/t²) residual. Only strictly one-sided starts bound all inverse squares by the two scalar envelopes. For irreducible W the stationary left-vector projection removes the simple Perron eigenvalue; every remaining eigenvalue has real part <1 even when W is periodic, so W−I on that subspace is exponentially stable under the vanishing transverse perturbation. The weighted mean has quadratic transverse error, hence its inverse-square derivative has at most O(t^{3/2} exp(−2ηt)) additional error; all node inverse squares differ from the mean's by o(1). W=I really can retain distinct constants: same-sign distinct scalar starts are nonzero time translates, shifting the constant by 8/3 times the time shift. In the nonstationary homogeneous variational equation all matrices commute. As an independent check, a(t)−1=g'(y(t)) and its integral is log|g(y(t))/g(y(0))|, giving exactly the −(3/2)log t term and a finite constant. This is a matrix factorization, not nonlinear mode decay, and works for Jordan blocks.
